Facility specific seeding pass 2026-09-02, batch 80 (Ark Data Centers missing-address campaign): applied 3401 Technology Drive, Duluth, sourced from convergence of a maximum confidence reverse geocode of this rows own coordinates and an independent, name specific aggregator listing for this operators Duluth 1 building. Noted but did not apply a third, conflicting aggregator address that matched neither known Duluth building nor this rows own coordinates.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] Per Ark Data Centers own site, this Duluth, Minnesota facility totals more than 26,000 square feet, with 10,000 square feet of conditioned data center space, 300 racks available, and provides 1,000 kW of power, Energy Star certified for a fifth consecutive year as of 2023. An earlier pass on file for this operator confirmed this brand is the current name for the former Involta brand at this same Duluth market, unrelated to a separate, larger batch of former Involta facilities this registry tracks in Ohio under the same corrected operator name. This session found the operator actually maintains two distinct Duluth buildings, per a data center industry aggregator directory, Duluth 1 at 3401 Technology Drive, Duluth, MN 55811, and Duluth 2 at 421 North 6th Avenue East, Duluth, MN 55805. Reverse geocoding this rows own stored coordinates through a third party service returned an exact match at the services maximum confidence level for the Duluth 1 address, 3401 Technology Drive, which this session applies given this convergence of a coordinate based method and an independent, name specific aggregator listing. A separate aggregator listing gave a third, different address, 4361 Rice Lake Road, for a facility it also labeled as this operators Duluth data center, but that address matches neither the Duluth 1 nor Duluth 2 listing and does not match this rows own reverse geocoded coordinates, so it is noted but not applied, and may reflect a stale or otherwise inaccurate aggregator entry.

reading.body:
Ark Duluth Data Center holds 300 racks across 10,000 square feet of conditioned space, drawing 1,000 kW of IT power. Assuming 3.3 kW per rack, a density typical of older enterprise colocation, this translates to roughly 300 racks of compute capacity. The facility is Energy Star certified as of 2023, qualifying it for efficient operation at that specification tier.

Minnesota has published power capacity at only 2 of 13 mapped data center facilities. Ark Duluth's 1 megawatt ranks second in the state among published figures, behind a 9 megawatt facility, and represents 10 percent of the state's total published data center capacity. No information on Minnesota's grid constraints or wholesale power access is published here.

This campus is too small to drive AI scaling decisions. A thousand kilowatts places it outside the emerging density tiers that matter for large language model training, where individual facilities now routinely exceed 100 megawatts. It serves regional colocation demand, a category disconnected from the accelerator procurement pipelines that consume grid capacity at scale.
